problem: Modular VLM+LLM agents use a goal-agnostic VLM description, so task-critical visual details are missed (perception-reasoning-decision gap). Prior QA-based methods rely on predefined or oracle questions/answers and concatenate the QA text into long, noisy prompts.
motivation: In humans, perception is driven by the goal, while current VLM-LLM pipelines decouple the two. Simply giving the goal to the VLM causes hallucinations. The paper wants a fully automatic feedback loop from the decision LLM to the VLM that produces compact, task-relevant descriptions and can still be trained with text-based RL recipes.
key_idea: The LLM critiques the VLM's initial scene description against the goal, generates questions, the VLM answers them, and the LLM synthesizes a compact task-driven description that the same LLM (with LoRA) uses to act, trained by BC then PPO.
insight: The gain comes from better perception content, not from modularity: raw-perception VLM+LLM is about equal to monolithic VLMs (70 vs 69 on ALFWorld). Goal-conditioning the VLM directly hurts (64% vs 69% raw) because it induces hallucinations, while QA-grounded interaction gives 75%. LLM synthesis beats concatenation (75 vs 72) and QA-only (70), and roughly halves prompt length (967 vs 1764 tokens on R2R). Generated questions are nearly as good as oracle questions (75 vs 77).
method: Initial description: the VLM (Idefics2-8B) gets the fixed prompt 'Describe the scene in detail' and outputs d_i.

Question generation: the frozen LLM (Mistral-7B or Qwen3-4B) sees d_i and goal g and asks 'Do you see ...' questions about missing information, or answers 'I have all the information'. On average 2-3 questions per step.
Visual QA: the VLM answers each question about the current image with a detailed explanation, not just yes/no.
Description refinement: the LLM merges d_i and the QA pairs into a single concise, confirmed-only description d_f, removing contradictions.
Decision policy: the same LLM with LoRA adapters (r=32, alpha=16 on Wq/Wv, active only for action generation) scores action-token likelihood given g, history H (5 transitions) and d_f.

Training: descriptions are precomputed once for BC on successful bot demonstrations (lr 1e-4). PPO (lr 5e-6, clip 0.1) follows with DQA active online, using a learned value function as in GLAM/Carta et al.

setting.backbone: Idefics2-8B (frozen VLM for perception) + Mistral-7B (frozen base for question generation and refinement; LoRA-tuned as policy); variant with Qwen3-4B as the LLM
setting.training_data: ALFWorld: 3,553 training episodes, successful rule-based bot trajectories for BC, then online PPO in the visual env. R2R: 14,039 training episodes, Dijkstra shortest-path bot demonstrations, BC only. No text-environment supervision.
setting.observation: RGB images (ALFWorld egocentric; R2R Front/Left/Right views described by the VLM)
setting.action_space: textual actions (ALFWorld text commands; R2R discrete Turn Left/Right, Move Forward, Stop)
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle Q/QA variants are used only as ablations; the parallel text env is used only to evaluate description quality)

numbers.extra: BC on R2R training set with Dijkstra bot demonstrations; no oracle questions
numbers.evidence: Table R2R: PRISM_BC (our) 6.23 / 65.38 / 46.08 / 43.14. Appendix: Val Unseen 2,349 episodes

numbers_note: ALFWorld is not in the canonical list, so it is labelled other:ALFWorld. The paper says 'out-of-distribution test sets' and the appendix lists the Val Unseen split with 134 episodes.
results: On ALFWorld, PRISM_BC+RL reaches 80% average SR, against 75% for VIPER_BC+RL, 69% for Idefics2 8B, and 21% for RL4VLM. It approaches text-supervised EMMA (82%) and EMAC+ (86%). On R2R, PRISM reaches SR 46.08, OSR 65.38, SPL 43.14, beating LangNav, NavGPT and DiscussNav (43 SR) on SR/OSR/SPL. Against the same-backbone DiscussNAV* reimplementation it gains more than 10 SR points (35.52 to 46.08), and NE improves from 7.66 to 6.23, though DiscussNAV's original 5.32 NE is lower.
limitations: Per-step latency is about 3x higher than raw perception (6.35 vs 2.14 s/step) because of three sequential passes, partly offset by fewer steps per episode (17.1 vs 20.9).
Generated questions rely on common sense and lack environment-specific priors, costing about 2 pt vs oracle questions; VLM answer errors of about 8% remain.
Evaluated only in ALFWorld and discrete-action R2R (no continuous control or real robot); R2R is BC only with a modest full-episode comparison to reported baselines.
builds_on: GLAM (Carta et al. LLM grounding with PPO)
